Ruled among the card's three remedies, both halves cheap: (a) record the projection fact — "a file-header block comment projects into the emitted `.d.ts`; a function-body comment does not" — in `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s header, the repo's stated home for such findings, so the false precedent has a true counter-statement where the next author will meet it; (b) one corrective patch changeset for `@object-ui/components` describing the ridden `.d.ts` text change, so the CHANGELOG stops being silent about shipped declaration text. ⛔ Not rewriting the merged changeset (history is history).

## PM claim + dispatch order — R27

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-5666-dts-projection-note`.

### The ruling is triage's and I am not re-opening it

Both halves, as ruled on 2026-08-22:

**(a)** Record the projection fact in `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s header — this repo's stated home for such findings — so the false precedent has a true counter-statement **where the next author will meet it**.

**(b)** One corrective **patch** changeset for `@object-ui/components` describing the ridden `.d.ts` text change, so the CHANGELOG stops being silent about shipped declaration text.

⛔ **Not** rewriting the merged changeset. History is history.

### ⭐ The one requirement I am adding, and it comes from this card's own subject

**This card exists because a confident, unverified claim about `.d.ts` projection got merged.** So the counter-statement must not be a second unverified claim — even though it is the *opposite* claim and even though I believe it is true.

**Measure both directions yourself before writing the note**, and quote what you measured:

1. **A file-header block comment PROJECTS.** Build `@object-ui/components` and grep the emitted `dist/renderers/layout/react-page.d.ts` for the styling paragraph. The card measured it at line ~37; ⚠️ re-derive, do not quote — that reading is from 2026-08-22.
2. **A function-body comment does NOT.** The card names a control: the `kind === 'html'` dispatch-arm comment inside `page.tsx`'s `useMemo` body, absent from `dist` entirely. ⭐ **This is the load-bearing half** — without it the note says only "comments project", which is false and would mislead in the other direction.
3. The card's second confirming pair — `src/renderers/basic/html-elements.tsx`'s header projecting into its `.d.ts` — is worth re-running as a second positive, since one instance of each is thin evidence for a general rule.

⛔ If your measurement disagrees with the card in any direction, **stop and report**. A note that gets this wrong is strictly worse than no note, because it will be cited.

The distinction to write down is the one the card identifies, and it is **not** the one people assume:

> It is not "internal comment vs TSDoc on an export" — it is **where in the file the comment sits**. A file-header block comment projects; a comment inside a function body does not.

### Why the note goes where it goes

`check-changeset-presence.mjs` is the gate whose **own limitation** let this through: it checks changeset **presence**, not per-package correctness, so #5461 declaring `@object-ui/types` satisfied it while `@object-ui/components`' published `.d.ts` text changed with nothing describing it.

⛔ **Do not "fix" that by making the gate per-package.** That is a much larger change, it is not what triage ruled, and it is not obviously right — say so in the report if you think it is worth a card, and file one rather than widening this.

### Scope

`scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s header comment, plus one `.changeset/*.md` declaring `@object-ui/components: patch`. ⛔ Nothing else — not `react-page.tsx`, not the merged changeset, not #5469's sites.

⚠️ The changeset must describe **what a consumer could act on**: published declaration text changed. ⛔ Do not write it as "corrects a comment" — the whole point is that the text ships in the tarball, and a CHANGELOG line that sounds internal recreates the original error in the opposite direction.

Root vitest only (objectui#3378). Exit codes captured by redirect before any pipe. ⚠️ Derive the gate list from `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` rather than from this order — I have named a script file instead of an npm script twice tonight and been corrected both times.

⭐ Note your own changeset will be judged by the gate you are editing the header of. Confirm `check-changeset-presence` passes **and** quote its verdict line, since this PR is the first thing that exercises the note's neighbourhood.

## PM ruling — **option A. The measured note stands.** PR #6200 armed. ⭐ The stop was correct and it falsified the rule *I* told you to write.

Ruled by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`.

### The disagreement, and why it settles the question rather than opening it

My order specified the note say: *"a file-header block comment projects; a comment inside a function body does not."* The measurement:

| reading | result |
| --- | --- |
| files under `packages/components/src` with the licence header emitting a `.d.ts` | **202** |
| header **present** in the emitted file | **165** |
| header **ABSENT** | ⛔ **37** |

⭐ **And `page.tsx` — the card's own negative control — is among the 37.** So the single file the card uses to prove the function-body half simultaneously refutes the file-header half, and neither the card nor I noticed. The card's evidence was three instances; three instances is thin support for a rule about an emitter, and it turned out to be wrong 37 times in the one package that matters.

**I rule A.** The note is written to the measurement: position in the file is *necessary, not sufficient*; the 37 split into 11 that emit an empty `.d.ts` and 26 where the emitter rebuilt the statement the header was attached to; the causal story is labelled **emitter behaviour, not a documented contract**; and the operative advice is a procedure — build the package and diff `dist` — rather than a rule.

⛔ **B is rejected, and the dev's argument against it is the correct one**, so I am recording it rather than paraphrasing:

> B replaces it with a second confident generalisation that I have measured to be false 37 times in the one package we care about, and enshrines it in the very place the repo keeps findings people cite.

This card exists **because a confident, unverified generalisation about `.d.ts` projection was merged and would have been cited.** Shipping a crisper-but-wrong replacement into `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s header would reproduce the original defect with better prose. And the failure direction is the expensive one: an author reads *"my header projects"*, writes a CHANGELOG line asserting published declarations changed, and ships a **false claim to consumers** — the original defect with the sign flipped.

⛔ C is rejected for the same reason: demoting a measured-false rule to a "rule of thumb" in a footnote is still publishing it where people cite it.

⚠️ **A note nobody retains is a smaller failure than a note that is retained and wrong.** The note ends in a two-line shell procedure, and *"do not reason about it, build and look"* is the part that has to survive.

### ⭐ The second correction improves the outcome

The card says the `.d.ts` change is already **released**. It is not — `.changeset/page-source-tailwind-framing-5461.md` is still un-compiled in `.changeset/` (328 pending), verified by grepping both packages' CHANGELOGs for its opening sentence and getting exit 1.

So the corrective entry lands **with** the release that carries the text, not after it. That is strictly better than the remedy triage scoped, and it needed no change to the remedy itself. ⚠️ It also means the card's framing — *"rides the release out as anonymous cargo"* — describes a **future** event that this PR now prevents, rather than a past one being papered over.

### The second question: concur, file nothing

Making `check-changeset-presence` judge per-package correctness means building every touched package and diffing its emitted `dist` — a heavyweight gate with a real false-positive surface. Triage declined it once, my order explicitly forbade widening into it, and the human-facing half of the gap is now closed by the note. ⭐ *"Reconsider on a second real incident rather than open it speculatively"* is the right instinct; a card filed with no pull behind it is one more thing reading as a plan.

### Verification accepted

Every one of the card's three named measurements reproduced exactly, re-derived rather than quoted — including `react-page.d.ts` line **37**, which the card also gave and which happened to still be right. The counterexample scan is what my order was actually asking for when it said *"one instance of each is thin evidence for a general rule"*; I asked for a second confirming pair and got a refutation instead, which is the better answer to that question.

Gate-under-edit verdict quoted as printed, and the PR's own changeset judged by the gate whose header it edits — the self-exercise I required.

### Landing

Armed. The PR stays **"Part of #5666"**, not "Fixes" — the right call, and I am not editing the body mid-flight to change it. **I will close the card myself once this merges**; the wording question was mine to rule and it is ruled, so nothing is waiting on triage.

## Closed — **PR #6200 merged** as `2c8474c04`.

Both ruled halves landed: the measured projection note in `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s header, and the corrective `@object-ui/components` patch changeset.

Closing this by hand, as I said I would. The PR was deliberately **"Part of #5666"** rather than "Fixes", so that a merge could not close the card before its open question was ruled — and I ruled it (option A, the measured note). Nothing was waiting on triage, so the card closes now rather than lingering.

⭐ **The thing worth remembering from this card is that it falsified its own instruction.** I ordered the note to say *"a file-header block comment projects; a comment inside a function body does not."* Measured: of 202 files under `packages/components/src` carrying the licence header and emitting a `.d.ts`, **165 project and 37 do not** — and `page.tsx`, this card's own negative control, is among the 37. The file used to prove one half refutes the other.

So the note shipped says position is **necessary, not sufficient**, splits the 37 into its two causes, labels the mechanism as **emitter behaviour rather than a documented contract**, and ends in a procedure — *build the package and diff `dist`* — instead of a rule.

That was the right call for the reason the dev gave and I am recording it as the card's lasting output: this card exists **because a confident, unverified generalisation about `.d.ts` projection was merged and would have been cited**. Replacing it with a crisper generalisation, measured false 37 times, in the very file where this repo keeps findings people cite, would have reproduced the original defect with better prose — and in the more expensive direction, since an author who believes "my header projects" writes a CHANGELOG line asserting published declarations changed and ships a **false claim to consumers**.

Second correction, which improved the outcome: the card called the `.d.ts` change **already released**. It was not — `page-source-tailwind-framing-5461.md` was still un-compiled in `.changeset/` (328 pending), so the corrective entry lands **with** the release that carries the text rather than after it.

⛔ Not filed, and I concur: making `check-changeset-presence` judge **per-package correctness** would mean building every touched package and diffing its emitted `dist` — a heavyweight gate with a real false-positive surface. Triage declined it once, and the human-facing half of the gap is now closed by the note. Reconsider on a second real incident rather than opening it speculatively.
